Match Ratings

Add the historical match-quality ratings from old Discord "top match" polls. These blend into the public star average on the Archive, and feed each wrestler's ★ average shown in the Rankings. Your live per-user star voting is untouched.

Pick an event, then for each match either type the stars directly OR enter the poll votes and click "Auto-stars" to compute them (top match in the event = 5★, others scaled down by vote share). "Voters/source" is shown publicly so people can see where the rating came from (e.g. "WCA 48 community poll").

Pick an event to load its matches.
Records rangeUnsaved

Only shows inside this range change records, rankings and contender points. Shows outside it keep their winners for Past Events, the Timeline and each profile's Match History, they just never touch a record. WCA 34 is where the current era starts.

Changing the range doesn't rewrite totals already recorded. It decides what can be recorded from now on, and which shows the site counts for "Going in" records and recent form. Anything already recorded from a show outside the range is listed below so you can take it back out.
Title reigns check

A defense = a match marked with that title in the match's Championship box, won by the champion, after the show they won it, up to the show they lost it. Defenses count from any show, even before the range. The W / L next to a reign only counts matches in that title's division, inside the records range above. For a faction title, the faction counts when its team name is on the side or two or more of its members team up. One member alone doesn't count. Reigns come from Title History (Won at / Lost at like "WCA 43"). "Vacated" ends at the next champion's show.

Set one match as LIVE so it appears in the "Current Match — LIVE" block on the site. People can still bet on it there if its betting is open. Clear it when the match ends.
Open a match to let players bet on it. Close it to lock all bets in as official. Matches you're still building can stay closed.
Recording a result writes the record books: the winning side gets a Win (+1 contender point if they're not the champion, max 3), whoever you mark as taking the fall (pinned/tapped) gets a Loss, and everyone else on a losing side gets a No-Win. Recent form, title changes, and title-shot contender resets all happen automatically, and every change is written to the Change Log tab. Made a mistake? Undo reverses everything exactly. Settling bets and recording results are separate — bets pay the viewers, results update the wrestlers.
This is the permanent action that writes history: it captures the event champion (highest balance), saves every bettor's final standing to the leaderboard, and adds their winnings to all-time totals. Settle or void every match first. If you're just testing, don't complete — use Delete below to remove the test event cleanly. You can Reopen a completed event to undo it.
Archive visibility & cleanup
Hide keeps the data but removes the event from the public archive. Delete is permanent — it wipes the event, its matches, all bets, and its standings, and rolls back any all-time winnings it added. Use Delete for test events.
Dashboard countdown
Shows a big countdown to the featured event's date/time on the public dashboard. Off by default — it never starts on its own, so creating or testing events won't trigger it. Turn it on only when you want fans to see it. (Purely visual — sends no alerts.)

After Action Report

The full betting breakdown for a show — every match, every bet, every player's ledger, and why they rank where they rank. Green = points won · red = points lost · white = neutral / baseline. The championship counts betting profit only — watch-time earnings never factor in here. You can open this mid-show to watch the race live, or after completing to verify the captured champion.
Not a gambling person? How to read this report
How a bet works here: every match has its own prize pool made from everyone's bets. Pick the winner and you get your bet back plus a slice of the money the losing side put in — the bigger your bet compared to the other winners, the bigger your slice. Pick wrong and your bet goes to the winners. That's it.

Why a "win" can pay small: if almost everyone bet the same (correct) side, there's barely any losing money to split — safe picks pay little. Longshot picks pay big because the losing pool is huge compared to the winning one. That's why someone can go 5-for-8 and still finish negative while someone who hit one big underdog finishes on top.

Special cases: if literally everyone picked the winner, there's nothing to split, so everyone gets their bet back plus a flat $250 bonus. If nobody picked the winner, every stake is simply lost — that's the risk of betting.

How the champion is decided: add up each player's green and red numbers for the show. Highest total profit wins. Baseline is $0 — everyone starts the show even, no matter how many points they walked in with, so a brand-new bettor can beat a 10-year veteran.

The verification panel below the banner recomputes everything from the raw bets and compares it to what got captured when you completed the event. Green shield = the math checks out and the champion is provably correct. Red warning = the stored numbers don't match the bets, and it tells you exactly where.

Channels

Rerun channels for the website's Watch Live page. They play whenever no show is live, and everyone on a channel watches the same moment, with the Live Chat beside it. When you go live, every channel stops and the page switches to the live show. When the show is over, press Stop following live in Show Results (or mark the show complete) and the channels come back on their own within about a minute. Requires SUPABASE_SETUP_tv_channels.sql to have been run once.

Customize every auto-post the bot sends. Edit the title, body, color, bot name, whether it pings @everyone, and whether it fires at all. Saved to your database — changes apply on the next post, no redeploy needed.

Placeholders you can drop into the body: {event} (event name), {match} (the matchup), {detail} (extra context). Discord markdown works: **bold**, *italic*, line breaks.

Restore from a backup file

Load a backup .json, review exactly what will change, then type the confirmation phrase to write it. Restore upserts rows (insert or overwrite by primary key); it never deletes rows that aren't in the file.
